meta.titre: Defects of Vision: short sight, long sight and astigmatism with their lens corrections
meta.sous_theme: Myopia, hypermetropia, astigmatism and their correction

sections.contenu_markdown: In a Form 5 class, one student sits near the front because the writing on the board is blurred for her, while another holds her book at arm's length to read. Both have an eye that does not focus light correctly on the retina. GCE questions ask you to name the defect, explain its cause and state the lens that corrects it. The key is to follow where the image forms in relation to the retina.

items: The retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye.
The cornea and the lens bend (refract) light to form an image on the retina.
A convex lens brings rays together, while a concave lens spreads them apart.

sections.titre: Focusing in the normal eye and the main defects of vision
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Focusing in a normal eye
Light is refracted by the cornea and the lens and forms a sharp, upside-down image on the retina. The lens changes shape to focus on near or distant objects. This is called **accommodation**.

| Looking at | Ciliary muscles | Suspensory ligaments | Lens |
|---|---|---|---|
| A near object | Contract | Slacken | Becomes thicker and more curved |
| A distant object | Relax | Become taut | Becomes thinner and flatter |

### The main defects

| Defect | Sees clearly | Blurred | Image forms | Cause | Correction |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Short sight (myopia) | Near objects | Distant objects | In front of the retina | Eyeball too long, or lens too strong | Concave (diverging) lens |
| Long sight (hypermetropia) | Distant objects | Near objects | Behind the retina | Eyeball too short, or lens too weak | Convex (converging) lens |
| Astigmatism | Nothing is fully sharp | Objects at any distance | In different places for different directions | Cornea (or lens) not evenly curved | Cylindrical lens |

A concave lens spreads the light slightly before it enters the eye, so the image is pushed back onto the retina. A convex lens brings the rays together a little before they enter, so the image moves forward onto the retina.

variantes.nom: Describing a defect: the four-point plan
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question says 'what is' or 'describe' a defect
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give four points in this order: what the person can and cannot see clearly, where the image forms, the cause, and the correction. This is enough to earn the marks for most 'what is' questions.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question mentions an older person or a cloudy lens
variantes.contenu_markdown: In **presbyopia** the lens of an older person becomes stiff and cannot become thicker, so near objects are blurred; reading glasses with convex lenses help. In a **cataract** the lens becomes cloudy so less light gets through; it is treated by an operation that replaces the lens with a clear artificial one.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When you must choose between convex and concave
variantes.contenu_markdown: Ask whether the image forms in front of or behind the retina. In front of the retina means the rays are bent too much, so a concave lens is needed. Behind the retina means the rays are not bent enough, so a convex lens is needed.

sections.enonce_markdown:
A student reads a book comfortably when it is 10 cm from her eyes, but she cannot read the writing on the board across the classroom.

(a) Name her defect.
(b) State where the image of the board forms.
(c) Give one cause.
(d) Name the type of lens that corrects the defect and say how it helps.

etapes.action: Decide what she sees well and what she does not.
etapes.justification: Clear near vision with blurred distant vision is the sign of short sight.

etapes.action: Place the image in relation to the retina.
etapes.justification: The rays from a distant object are focused too strongly, so they meet before they reach the retina.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The image forms in front of the retina.

etapes.justification: Either the eyeball is longer than normal, so the retina is too far back, or the lens is too strong.

etapes.action: Choose the lens and explain it.
etapes.justification: The rays are bent too much, so they have to be spread slightly first.
etapes.resultat_markdown: A concave (diverging) lens, which pushes the image back onto the retina.

sections.conclusion_markdown: (a) **Short sight (myopia)**. (b) **In front of the retina**. (c) **The eyeball is too long** (or the lens is too strong). (d) **A concave lens**, which spreads the rays a little so the image forms on the retina.

items.erreur_markdown: A short-sighted person cannot see near objects.
items.pourquoi_faux: A short-sighted person sees near objects clearly and distant objects blurred.
items.correction_markdown: Myopia: near objects clear, distant objects blurred.

items.erreur_markdown: Long sight is corrected with a concave lens.
items.pourquoi_faux: In long sight the image forms behind the retina and the rays must be brought together, which a convex lens does.
items.correction_markdown: Long sight: convex lens. Short sight: concave lens.

items.erreur_markdown: In short sight the image forms behind the retina.
items.pourquoi_faux: It forms in front of the retina because the eye bends the light too strongly for the length of the eyeball.
items.correction_markdown: Short sight: image in front of the retina. Long sight: image behind the retina.

items.erreur_markdown: Astigmatism is blindness in one eye.
items.pourquoi_faux: It is a blurring caused by an unevenly curved cornea or lens, and it can be corrected with a cylindrical lens.
items.correction_markdown: Astigmatism is uneven curvature of the cornea or lens, which causes blurred vision at all distances.

items.erreur_markdown: The lens becomes thinner when we look at a close object.
items.pourquoi_faux: To look at near objects the ciliary muscles contract, the suspensory ligaments slacken and the lens becomes thicker.
items.correction_markdown: Near object: thicker lens. Distant object: thinner lens.

items.enonce_markdown: A 12-year-old girl sees the board clearly but has to hold a book far from her eyes to read it. Name her defect and the lens that corrects it. Say where the image of the book forms.
items.solution_markdown: She has **long sight (hypermetropia)**. The image of a near object forms **behind the retina**. It is corrected with a **convex lens**.

items.enonce_markdown:
ONE or MORE of the responses below is (are) correct.

Long sight

1. Forms the image behind the retina.
2. Makes distant objects clearer than near ones.
3. Is corrected by a concave lens.

Choose: A) all three; B) 1 and 2 only; C) 2 and 3 only; D) 1 only.
items.solution_markdown: 1 is true: the image forms behind the retina. 2 is true: a long-sighted person sees distant objects better than near ones. 3 is false: a convex lens is needed. Statements 1 and 2 only are correct. Answer: **B**.

items.enonce_markdown:
(a) Explain how an eyeball that is longer than normal makes the writing on a distant board blurred.
(b) Explain how a concave lens corrects this.
(c) Describe what happens to the lens and to the ciliary muscles when a person looks from a distant tree to a book.
(d) A person's vision is blurred at every distance and the cornea is found to be unevenly curved. Name the defect and the lens used.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) The lens and cornea bring the light from the distant board to a point before the retina, because the retina is too far back. The light spreads out again, so a blurred image falls on the retina.
(b) The concave lens spreads the rays slightly before they enter the eye, so the eye focuses them further back, **on the retina**.
(c) The ciliary muscles **contract**, the suspensory ligaments slacken and the lens becomes **thicker and more curved**.
(d) **Astigmatism**, corrected with a **cylindrical lens**.

items_markdown: Short sight: near objects clear, distant objects blurred; image in front of the retina; concave lens.
Long sight: distant objects clear, near objects blurred; image behind the retina; convex lens.
Astigmatism is caused by an unevenly curved cornea or lens and is corrected with a cylindrical lens.
For near objects the ciliary muscles contract and the lens becomes thicker; for distant objects the reverse happens.
To answer a 'what is' question, give what is seen clearly, where the image forms, the cause and the correction.
